paragraphs: Mentioned at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Chagigah, chapter 2, where Rabbi Haggai reported in his name.
In Vayikra Rabbah26:7, Rabbi Huna reported in his name.

notes.text: The first citation does not name the Jerusalem Talmud tractate. The opening chapter2 locator is translated, but its tractate remains unresolved.

The saved named Guggenheimer Chagigah 2:1 paragraph explicitly has Rabbi Haggai reporting Rabbi Yabetz, supplying the unnamed tractate. The connected passage in saved Torat Emet Vayikra Rabbah 26:7 explicitly has Rav Huna reporting Yabetz, contradicting the earlier research claim that the name was absent. Hyman’s Rabbi Huna title is retained against that witness’s Rav. These matches establish textual comparisons, not broader identities.

The printed entry (Hyman, vol. II, p. 769) gives only the beginning of chapter 2 of the Jerusalem Talmud. Guggenheimer’s Chagigah 2:1 names Rabbi Haggai twice in Rabbi Yabetz’s name. The Torat Emet text of Vayikra Rabbah 26:7 has the parallel teachings in Yabetz’s name from Rav Huna. Hyman uses the abbreviation for Rabbi in his notice.
